tool.name: subdomain_takeover_check
tool.description:
Check subdomains for takeover candidates against a known-provider fingerprint matrix.
For each subdomain, follow CNAMEs and match the final target against a list of ~38 third-party services known to be vulnerable to subdomain takeover when the underlying project / bucket / app is unclaimed. Covers GitHub Pages, Heroku, AWS S3 / CloudFront / API Gateway, Vercel, Netlify, Fastly, Statuspage, Surge.sh, Pantheon, Tilda, Helpjuice, Cargocollective, Fly.io, Render, Intercom, Thinkific, Teachable, Zendesk, Wishpond, Aha.io, Acquia, Canny.io, AfterShip, Launchrock, DigitalOcean Apps, Firebase Hosting, Google Sites, Uberflip, Smartling, Bitbucket, Ghost, Shopify, Tumblr, WordPress, ReadMe, Azure CloudApp.
When the CNAME matches a provider, fetch the subdomain over HTTP and check the response body for that provider's "unclaimed" signature.
Conservative — flags candidates only. Active verification (claim the project, confirm exploit) is intentionally out of scope.
Findings are filed under category `subdomain_takeover` with severity tied to provider impact (`high` for hijack-friendly providers like Heroku, GitHub Pages; `medium` for ambiguous like Vercel where 404 doesn't always mean takeover). `verification_status` is "verified" when the fingerprint matched the response body, "pattern_match" when only the CNAME matched.
Use AFTER subdomain enumeration: pass the discovered subdomain list via `subdomains`. When called with only the apex `domain`, only the apex is checked.

parameter.name: domain
parameter.description: Apex domain (e.g. "example.com"). Used as fallback when `subdomains` not given.

parameter.name: subdomains
parameter.description: Comma-separated list of fully-qualified subdomains to check, e.g. "blog.example.com,api.example.com,www.example.com". When omitted, only the apex is checked.

returns.description: {success, domain, checked, candidates, results: [...]}. Each result has {host, cname, candidate, provider, verification_status, severity}.
